module_title: Advanced Analysis - Rift Valleys, Faults, and Coastal Plains
introduction: This advanced level explores the structural faults that shaped the plateau, the micro-divisions of the Central Highlands, and the critical differences between the Eastern and Western coastal plains.

core_concepts.title: The Malda Fault
core_concepts.description: During the movement of the Indian plate, a huge fault was created between the Rajmahal hills and the Meghalaya plateau. This 'Malda Fault' was later filled by the Ganga-Brahmaputra deposits. This is why Meghalaya is physically separated from the main Peninsula.

core_concepts.title: Sub-divisions of Central Highlands
core_concepts.description: Moving West to East: Malwa Plateau (volcanic origin), Bundelkhand (granite and gneiss, highly eroded), Baghelkhand, and the Chotanagpur Plateau (rich in coal and iron ore, drained by the Damodar river).

core_concepts.title: The Deccan Trap
core_concepts.description: Formed at the end of the Cretaceous period due to 'fissure volcanic eruption'. The basaltic lava spread over vast areas, forming step-like structures (Traps). Weathering of these rocks formed the Regur (Black) soil.

core_concepts.title: Western vs. Eastern Coastal Plains
core_concepts.description: The Western Coastal Plain is 'submerged', making it narrow and ideal for natural ports (like Mumbai). Rivers here form Estuaries. The Eastern Coastal Plain is 'emergent', making it broader and characterized by large river Deltas (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery).

important_entities.name: Chotanagpur Plateau
important_entities.significance: Due to its massive reserves of minerals (coal, iron, mica), it is compared to the mineral-rich Ruhr valley of Germany.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Why Narmada and Tapi do not form Deltas
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Despite being large rivers, they flow west into the Arabian Sea and form Estuaries, not Deltas. Why? Because they flow through hard rocky rift valleys and carry almost no alluvium/sediment to deposit at their mouths.

The general tilt of the Peninsular Plateau is from West to East (which is why most rivers flow east into the Bay of Bengal). Narmada and Tapi flow west *against* this tilt because they are confined within rift valleys created by block faulting.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Konkan Coast (Maharashtra/Goa) -> Kannad Coast (Karnataka) -> Malabar Coast (Kerala).

exam_strategy_tips: In Assertion-Reasoning questions, perfectly align the 'Submerged' nature of the Western coast with the presence of 'Natural Harbors' and 'Estuaries'.
Remember the Damodar River flows through a rift valley in the Chotanagpur plateau, similar to Narmada and Tapi.
